UPDATE: Sebokeng handover (CBMADT) 2024

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We close the circle on our most ambitious project yet, as the Trust hands over a unique paediatric emergency centre at Sebokeng Hospital.

Unique Selling Point:
The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust has a longstanding relationship with Sebokeng Hospital. Now, we've completed a first-of-its-kind trauma facility that is being handed over to save the lives of Sedibeng's children.

Summary:
In the last decade, the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust has built two paediatric high-care wards at Sebokeng. But they’re operating beyond capacity. So the Trust stepped in again. In 2023, construction began on a brand new centre dedicated to triaging and treating paediatric emergencies. Thanks to this centre - first of its kind in a South African state hospital - children will no longer need to share the adult casualty, where they are often retraumatised, and don't have access to the specialised treatment and equipment that can make a difference to their health. This week, the Trust proudly unveils the completed, state-of-the-art facility, and hands it over to the hospital and its community.

Extra Budget Items:
Drone for before and after shots of the new facility.

Press Release:


The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust has a longstanding relationship with Sebokeng Regional Hospital. In the last decade, the Trust has built two paediatric high-care wards at Sebokeng, but they’re operating beyond capacity. Meanwhile, at Sebokeng as at other regional hospitals, children are traumatised by their exposure to violence and illness in the emergency department they share with the community's adults. So the Trust stepped in again. In 2023, construction began on a first-of-its-kind Paediatric Emergency Unit, where children will be treated by specialist doctors using equipment designed for their tiny bodies. This week, the Trust proudly unveiled the completed, state-of-the-art facility, and handed it over to the hospital, its community, and most importantly, its children.

Script:


VOICEOVER: Last December, Constance Bajomo of Sakhiwo Health Solutions gave us a tour of a raw construction site…
UPSOUND CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: Constance Bajomo: As the parent come in with the sick child, there is a nurse station there…
VOICEOVER: …squeezed between the dilapidated buildings of Sebokeng Regional Hospital.
UPSOUNDl: CLAIRE MAWISA: That was when this didn’t exist.
VOICEOVER: Today, we’re back…
UPSOUND: CLAIRE MAWISA: Walk me through what we are seeing.
CONSTANCE BAJOMO: This is the reception… these are our treatment spaces.
VOICEOVER: …to witness its transformation into a first-of-its-kind paediatric emergency unit…
UPSOUND: CONSTANCE BAJOMO: This is where the nurses will sit or stand, observing these treatment beds.
VOICEOVER: …now complete.
UPSOUND: CLAIRE MAWISA: The day is here, it’s happening!
CONSTANCE BAJOMO: It’s happening and we’re very excited to be part of it.
UPSOUND: MAKIBITI MADOLO: Our Accident and Emergencies are full at all times. Adult diseases, trauma, stabbing, gunshots… A child will come with a small broken bone but now is exposed to this environment.
VOICEOVER: Mrs Makibiti Madolo is the CEO of Sebokeng Regional Hospital.
UPSOUND: MAKIBITI MADOLO: Let’s separate them so they can have their free and own A&E where they can be children.
LINK: Less than a year ago, this was an empty shell, and we had to use a lot of imagination to see what it could be. Now the architects’ plans have come to life, but it’s been a very long, very stressful journey to get here.
VOICEOVER: The project was faced with one challenge after another. From soil conditions…
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: We couldn't do just a normal strip foundation due to the soil not being able to carry the loads from the building.
VOICEOVER: … to the construction mafia.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: They do come in groups of three, four people at a time, trying to intimidate us.
VOICEOVER: But on a bright hot day this week, all that is (almost) forgotten.
LINK: Today is a big day. Arriving behind me are representatives from government, the hospital, Multichoice and our donors to see the new unit being handed over to the province. But you’ll have to excuse me, because I’ve got a job to do!
UPSOUND: CLAIRE MAWISA: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen! My name is Claire Mawisa. Today is a day for celebration…
VOICEOVER: This unit is the latest triumph for the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust.
UPSOUND: NOMSA PHILISO: All the partners that join us today, they share the same value of wanting to do that which is good and better for South Africa.
VOICEOVER: The Trust has built over 20 facilities for children in state hospitals around the country since 2008. This is the third paediatric facility that the Trust has built at Sebokeng, which serves 1.3 million people in southern Gauteng.
LINK: A project like this costs millions, of course. But the donations are worth so much more than their rand value. A unit like this would simply not come into being without the generosity, patience and sheer determination to make it work.
UPSOUND: TASOULLA HURWITZ: We offered anything we could offer to make this project happen. And it has!
VOICEOVER: Tasoulla Hurwitz is the CEO of LottoStar, which provided the huge capital donation needed to get the project out of the ground.
UPSOUND: TASOULLA HURWITZ: How this all came along for us was I needed a birthday present for my husband.
CLAIRE MAWISA: Oh!
TASOULLA HURWITZ: And now we’ve decided in our family, kids and all, and company, we’re going to pay it forward.
CLAIRE MAWISA: Tell me, how does it feel, after three long years, at this moment?
TASOULLA HURWITZ: It’s worth every single effort, cent, whatever you want to call it. Now these moms around this area can actually get the best for their kiddies.
UPSOUND: CLINTON SOUTTER: Being a parent myself I understand what it’s like to have a young child that’s ill.
VOICEOVER: Clinton Soutter is the National Sales Manager of Franke, which donated luxury custom stainless steel-ware for the whole facility.
UPSOUND: CLINTON SOUTTER: Our business has got over a hundred years of building products serving this country. And for us to be involved in a project like this is personal. It’s about making that real difference to people who come in here and need hope.
UPSOUND: TANDY COLEMAN: Children in hospital is hard and you want a space where they feel happy and then you want a space also where their parents can feel like they are safe and happy – or as happy as they can be, being in hospital.
VOICEOVER: Tandy Coleman is CEO of Polyflor, which provided medical-grade vinyl flooring, as well as custom wall art.
UPSOUND: TANDY COLEMAN: The best part of it is, someone comes up with an idea. And then we bring in the floor which is just the pallette on which to build and when I look around here today it is a beautiful palette on which to build.
LINK: This building is designed for children in every way – from specialist staff to equipment designed specifically for tiny bodies. It even has a playground.
UPSOUND: MAKIBITI MADOLO: It is a disruptive change to us. It challenges us to do better. It means that we are capable of looking after the assets that have been entrusted to us. And we hope the Trust will remain and grow.
